Fixture: 31_icc_rgb_32x32_lossless.jxl (+ 31_icc_rgb_32x32_lossless.icc)
32x32 RGB, mathematically lossless, with a hand-built matrix-shaper
ICC profile -- the E.4.4 tagcode-2/3 grouping case

Purpose
-------
Targets slice 4 (18181-1 E.4). The profile is a classic ICC v2
matrix-shaper: desc, rXYZ/gXYZ/bXYZ (three consecutive 20-byte XYZType
payloads), one rTRC curve *shared* by gTRC and bTRC, wtpt and cprt.

That shape is what E.4.4's two grouping tagcodes exist for: tagcode 3
emits rXYZ plus gXYZ and bXYZ at consecutive offsets, and tagcode 2 emits
rTRC plus gTRC and bTRC sharing one offset and size. A decoder that
emitted only the named tag would produce a tag table three entries short
and a size field that no longer matches, which is what
`every_decoded_profile_is_self_consistent` in tests/e2e_icc.rs checks.

Provenance
----------
  Encoder:      cjxl v0.13.0 196a43d9 [_AVX2_,SSE4,SSE2] {GNU 15.2.0}
  libjxl rev:   196a43d996aa6ed33ebf98812a7c6d43b2b6d01b (v0.12-snapshot-2-g196a43d9)
  cjxl flags:   -d 0 -e 3 -x icc_pathname=<profile>
  Built by:     tools/setup-oracles.sh (flags recorded in
                tools/oracle-bin/PINNED_REVISIONS.txt)
  Regenerate:   tools/make-icc-fixtures.sh
                That script IS the recipe; it rewrites the profile and the
                source and re-encodes.

  ICC profile:  tests/fixtures/generated/icc_rgb_matrix.icc  (456 bytes)
                sha256 d7e0c683e9587d92477c85e1505397c44c70f3cb8d780d95872ba83be7cf415f
                Synthetic. Built byte by byte by the Python snippet inside
                tools/make-icc-fixtures.sh from the ICC.1 structure (128-byte
                header, tag table, tag payloads). No system profile, no
                third-party profile and no colour-management library was read,
                converted or consulted, so this carries no licence beyond this
                repository's own.

  Source image: tests/fixtures/generated/src_icc_rgb_32x32.ppm  (3085 bytes)
                sha256 dd47bb59a185edff496673cfdafab164d2d9f27582c227d40012be48a383d0ac
                Synthetic, written by the Python snippet inside
                tools/make-icc-fixtures.sh -- no third-party image was used,
                converted or consulted.
                32x32 8-bit RGB (PPM P6):
                  R = x * 255 / 31        ramp along x
                  G = y * 255 / 31        ramp along y
                  B = (x + y) * 4 mod 256 diagonal sawtooth

  Fixture:      31_icc_rgb_32x32_lossless.jxl, 547 bytes
                sha256 f94d876609f28fa204064f23d80289d06c51fdef96b070306978f9fc990e5758

  Reference:    31_icc_rgb_32x32_lossless.icc, 456 bytes
                sha256 d7e0c683e9587d92477c85e1505397c44c70f3cb8d780d95872ba83be7cf415f
                A byte-identical copy of the ICC profile above, checked in so
                that tests/e2e_icc.rs can assert byte-exactness without an
                oracle installed.

Verification
------------
tools/make-icc-fixtures.sh checks two things on every run, and refuses to
write the fixture if either fails:

  * djxl --orig_icc_out returns a profile byte-identical to the one cjxl was
    given, so the reference really is what the codestream stores;
  * djxl decodes the pixels to a PNM byte-identical to the source, so the
    stream is mathematically lossless.

tests/e2e_icc.rs then asserts that JPXL's own E.4 decoder reproduces the
reference byte for byte, and repeats the comparison against a live djxl when
one is installed.

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change.
